extracted.intended_audience: press officers, institutional media relations staff, science communicators, and researchers submitting press releases to EurekAlert!
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and eligibility standards for submitting science-focused press releases and announcements to the EurekAlert! newswire, including timing, embargo rules, acceptable content categories, and multimedia restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core Timeliness Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Content must describe information "first made public within 90 days of content submission." For publications with multiple dates, the most recent applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures material is recent; when a work has multiple public-release dates, use the most recent date to determine eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargoes are permitted only when set by journal publishers or scientific meeting organizers announcing initial public release. Embargoes are prohibited if information is already publicly available or unrelated to publications, meetings, or press events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only honor embargoes originating from journals or meeting organizers for an initial public release; do not accept author-imposed embargoes for content already public or for items not tied to a publication/meeting/press event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible: Peer-Reviewed Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies in peer-reviewed journals, completed clinical trials, and peer-reviewed editorials/commentaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes research articles and peer-reviewed commentary when they represent an initial public disclosure or finalized, peer-reviewed results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible: Reports & Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific meeting presentations, government reports, clinical trial phase completions, validated survey data, and new research databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers work announced via meetings, official reports, validated datasets, and formal proceedings when they represent substantive scientific output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible: Business Announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Collaborations, mergers, regulatory approvals, clinical trial launches, forecasts, and policy statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business and organizational developments are acceptable when they have clear scientific, clinical, or policy relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible: Meeting Announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Upcoming or recently-held scientific meetings with media/public access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements must be for meetings that are accessible to media or the public and relate directly to scientific content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible: Grants & Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding announcements and award nomination calls with societal impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding and award news that have demonstrable scientific or societal significance are permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible: Book Announcements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements of books that are substantively about science are acceptable for the newswire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Unpublished research undergoing peer review; opinion-based editorials lacking peer-reviewed support; speeches and non-press-release formats; potentially biased findings with undisclosed conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit items that are still under peer review, are purely opinion without peer-reviewed evidence, are not in press-release format (e.g., speeches), or where conflicts of interest suggest bias and are not disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All images, videos, and audio must be cleared for third-party distribution. Stock image content is prohibited. AI-generated multimedia is ineligible except in documented AI/machine learning research cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only media for which third-party distribution rights are documented; do not use stock images; only accept AI-generated media when it is part of an explicitly documented AI/ML research example.
